claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 is an as-cast high-entropy alloy with an experimentally characterized hierarchical heterostructure.
The proposed model is a transformer-based machine-learning model combining compositional data with spatial phase maps, grain-boundary attributes, and heterointerface density.
Transformer models can capture intricate elemental interactions in HEAs through self-attention.
Transformer attention applied to high-resolution spatial descriptors will capture multiscale interactions governing stress distributions and crack propagation.
Spatial phase maps, grain-boundary characteristics, and heterointerface density mediate deformation and fracture in HfNbTiVAl10.
Adding detailed microstructural features will improve the mapping between microstructure and macroscopic mechanical response.
The proposed model will predict Young's modulus in HfNbTiVAl10 with approximately 10–15% relative error.
The proposed model will predict yield strength in HfNbTiVAl10 with approximately 10–15% relative error.
The proposed model will predict fracture-onset behavior in HfNbTiVAl10 with approximately 10–15% relative error.
The proposed model will be more accurate for these properties than traditional continuum or simplified multiscale simulations.
Transformer-based HEA models can improve prediction of elongation and ultimate tensile strength relative to random forests and Gaussian processes.
The proposed model will reduce prediction time from hours to minutes relative to established simulations.
Current continuum and simplified multiscale simulations do not sufficiently integrate hierarchical microstructural detail.
Inaccurate or insufficiently resolved microstructural descriptors may cause the model to fail.
A significant difference between the characterized microstructure and the microstructure present during testing may cause the model to fail.
Limited HEA training data may impair model robustness and generalization.
Transfer learning from synthetic materials data can mitigate scarcity of experimental HEA data.
Independent specimens will be evaluated using high-resolution imaging, tensile testing, fracture analysis or digital image correlation, and prediction-time measurements.
The hypothesis is predeclared as falsified if any predicted property differs from an independent measurement by more than 15%.
The hypothesis is also predeclared as falsified if computation remains on the order of hours rather than showing a marked reduction.
